Based on my search, I can provide you with comprehensive information about food temperature acceptance and safety standards.

## Food Temperature Acceptance Standards

### The Temperature Danger Zone

The most critical concept in food safety is the **"Temperature Danger Zone"** — the range where bacteria grow rapidly:

- **US Standard (FDA/USDA)**: 40°F to 140°F (4°C to 60°C)
- **ServSafe/Commercial US**: 41°F to 135°F (5°C to 57°C)
- **Australian Standard**: 5°C to 60°C

Bacteria can double in as little as **20 minutes** within this range, making temperature control essential.

---

### Acceptable Temperatures for Food Receipt/Acceptance

When **receiving or accepting food deliveries**, foods must already be at safe temperatures:

| Food Type | Acceptable Temperature at Receipt |
|-----------|-----------------------------------|
| **Cold/refrigerated foods** (dairy, meat, produce) | **41°F (5°C) or below** |
| **Frozen foods** | **0°F (-18°C) or below** (solid frozen, no thawing) |
| **Hot foods** | **135°F (57°C) or above** |
| **Fresh produce** (non-TCS foods) | Room temperature acceptable if not cut/peeled |

---

### Safe Holding Temperatures After Acceptance

Once accepted, foods must be maintained at:

| Category | Temperature Requirement |
|----------|------------------------|
| **Cold holding** | 40°F (4°C) or below |
| **Hot holding** | 135°F (57°C) or above |
| **Frozen storage** | 0°F (-18°C) or below |

---

### Safe Cooking/Internal Temperatures

Foods must reach these minimum internal temperatures for at least 15 seconds:

| Food | Minimum Internal Temperature |
|------|------------------------------|
| Poultry, stuffing, dishes with cooked TCS food | **165°F (74°C)** |
| Ground meat, injected meats, eggs held for service | **155°F (68°C)** |
| Seafood, steaks, chops, roast meats | **145°F (63°C)** |
| Fruits, vegetables, grains, legumes | **135°F (57°C)** |

---

### Key Rules for Food Acceptance

1. **Reject any delivery** where cold foods arrive above 41°F (5°C)
2. **Reject frozen foods** that show signs of thawing or are above 0°F (-18°C)
3. **Reject hot foods** that have fallen below 135°F (57°C)
4. **Check temperatures** with a calibrated thermometer — don't rely on touch or appearance
5. **Document temperatures** upon receipt for HACCP compliance

---

### Time Limits in the Danger Zone

If food enters the danger zone:

| Total Time in Danger Zone | Action Required |
|---------------------------|-----------------|
| **0–2 hours** | Use or return to proper temperature |
| **2–4 hours** | Use immediately (cannot return to refrigeration) |
| **Over 4 hours** | **Discard** — do not serve |

---

Sources:
1. https://www.webstaurantstore.com/article/29/following-food-safety-temperatures.html
2. https://thermalog.com.au/australian-food-safety-standards-a-guide-to-temperature-compliance/
3. https://ladle.com/resources/blog/safe-food-temperatures-protect-public-health-and-your-bottom-line/
4. https://www.rotomouldedproducts.com/news/what-are-the-key-temperature-requirements-for-safe-food-transportation-according-to-international-st-244097.html
5. https://www.tempcontrolpack.com/knowledge/temperature-standards-for-coldchain-logistics/
6. https://dutyfront.com/legal-standards-for-food-storage-temperature/
